unified.loginBody: Sign in with your parent account to follow tasks, lessons and family moments.
unified.signupBody: A parent creates the account. Your child does not need an email address.
unified.resetBody: Enter your parent account email. We will send a link to reset your password.
unified.childDeviceTitle: Will your child use this device?
unified.childDeviceBody: Connect a separate phone or tablet to your family. To share your own phone, sign in and use Child mode.
unified.familyCreateHelp: If you are the first parent to use GINA, create your family. You can invite another parent later.
unified.familyJoinHelp: If another parent has already created your family, enter their 8-character invitation code from Settings → My family. This is not a child device pairing code.
unified.settingsBody: Manage your family, child devices and account security.
unified.inviteHelp: Your partner enters this 8-character code in Settings → Family → Families and partner invitation. If they have no family yet, choose “Join a family by invitation” after signing in.
unified.childrenHelp: Each child has their own tasks, school timetable and stars.
unified.childPinHelp: This 4-digit code opens your child’s profile. Share it with your child. Set a new one here if it is forgotten.
unified.parentPinHelp: This 4-digit code protects the return from Child mode to the parent area on your phone. Keep it private. It is separate from your account password and child PIN.
unified.pinSaved: Your new PIN is saved. Use this code from now on.
unified.childAdded: Child profile added. Set a child PIN in their profile settings.
unified.pairIntro: Use this only for your child’s separate phone or tablet. Pairing connects that device to your family; it does not create a parent account.
unified.pairStep1: Open GINA on the child device. On the sign-in screen, tap “Connect a child device”.
unified.pairStep2: Tap “Create pairing code”. Enter the 6-digit code shown there below.
unified.pairStep3: After pairing, select who may use this device and whether a child PIN is required.
unified.pairSaved: Device connected. You can now select a profile on the child device.
unified.samePhoneBody: No pairing is needed to share your phone. Set your parent PIN in Security and your child’s PIN in their profile settings first.
unified.pairTitle: Connect this device to your family
unified.pairBody: This screen is for a separate phone or tablet used by a child. Have the parent’s phone nearby.
unified.pairChildStep1: Create a pairing code for this device.
unified.pairChildStep2: On the parent phone, open Settings → Child devices and enter this code.
unified.pairChildStep3: Once connected, choose your profile. If this device requires a PIN, enter your four-digit child PIN.
unified.deviceNameHint: For example: Ece’s tablet. Your parent sees this name in the connected devices list.
unified.childPinInstruction: Enter the 4-digit child PIN your parent set for you. If you forget it, your parent can reset it in Settings → My family → Profile settings.
unified.parentPinFirstBody: Leaving Child mode requires a private parent PIN. Set your 4-digit code in Security, then select your child’s profile.
unified.deviceRemoveHelp: Removing this connection stops the device accessing family information. Pair it again if you want to use it later.
unified.provaBody: Support learning with short practice sessions. Prepare an exercise, let your child complete it in their space and review the results together.

unified.questionHelp: Add your own question and correct answer to the library.
unified.generateHelp: Choose a topic and grade; review the generated questions before use.
unified.levelHelp: Explore the starting level with questions across topics.
unified.progressHelp: Review topic progress from completed activities.
unified.bookletHelp: Prepare questions as a printable booklet.

blueprintFlow.intro: Enter the topics and question counts from the scenario announced by the school. This creates a reusable distribution, not questions.
blueprintFlow.subjectHelp: Choose a timetable subject or enter its name.
blueprintFlow.rowHelp: Add one row per topic. Keep outcomes assessed together in a single question in the same row; do not multiply its count.
blueprintFlow.sourceHelp: Optional HTTPS link. Providing a link does not verify its content.
blueprintFlow.validHelp: Complete the name, consecutive academic years and distinct topic rows. Up to 30 questions in total.
blueprintFlow.manualNotice: This is your entered distribution, not an official curriculum record verified by GINA. We do not choose the school scenario automatically.
blueprintFlow.confirm: I checked the topics, grade and exam details against the school announcement.
blueprintFlow.savedHelp: Select this scenario when preparing a Prova for the same grade and subject. No questions have been generated or assigned yet.
blueprintFlow.pending: We will check the earlier save using the same request. A duplicate scenario will not be created.
blueprintFlow.errors.blueprint_invalid: Check distinct topics, consecutive academic years and the 30-question limit.
blueprintFlow.errors.blueprint_grade_mis: The child’s grade changed. Reopen this screen and try with the current grade.
blueprintFlow.errors.forbidden: You cannot change this child or family. Check your session.
blueprintFlow.errors.request_conflict: This request was used for different content. No new scenario was created. Contact support.
blueprintFlow.errors.unknown: The save outcome has not been confirmed. Retry to check the same request.
prova.ai.errors.blueprint_invalid: Check scenario topics and counts: up to 30 questions, with no missing or duplicate rows.
